facts.en: Temperatures on the Moon go from hotter than 121 °C in sunlight to colder than -246 °C in shadowed polar craters.
facts.pt: Na Lua a temperatura vai de mais de 121 °C ao sol até menos de -246 °C nas crateras sempre à sombra perto dos polos.
facts.quote: Surface temperatures on the Moon range from higher than 250°F to lower than -410°F.
facts.source: NASA Science: Weather on the Moon

facts.en: A full Moon day (sunrise to sunrise) lasts about 29.5 Earth days, so a long night can last around two weeks.
facts.pt: Um dia completo na Lua (de nascer do Sol a nascer do Sol) dura cerca de 29,5 dias da Terra, então uma noite pode durar umas duas semanas.
facts.quote: 29.5 days to change from new moon to new moon
facts.derived: ‘about two weeks of night’ = half of 29.5 days (our arithmetic).

facts.en: At the south pole the Sun stays very low (never more than about 7° above the horizon), so shadows are long and solar panels must point sideways.
facts.pt: No polo sul o Sol fica muito baixo (nunca mais de uns 7° acima do horizonte), então as sombras são longas e os painéis solares ficam de lado.
facts.quote: sun elevation in sky is never higher than about 7°
facts.source: NASA Technical Reports Server: lunar south pole lighting presentation (2023)

facts.en: The Moon has hardly any air and no global magnetic field, so nothing blocks space radiation. Your base must make its own shield.
facts.pt: A Lua quase não tem ar nem campo magnético global, então nada bloqueia a radiação do espaço. A base precisa do seu próprio escudo.
facts.quote: The Moon has hardly any atmosphere and no global magnetic field to shield it from space radiation.
facts.source: NASA Science: Weather on the Moon

facts.en: The ground is covered in charcoal-gray powdery dust that sticks to everything, even solar panels.
facts.pt: O chão é coberto por uma poeira cinza-escura bem fininha que gruda em tudo, até nos painéis solares.
facts.quote: covered by a rubble pile of charcoal-gray, powdery dust

facts.en: The Moon is about 384,400 km away, so a radio message takes about 1.3 seconds each way. Earth can help you almost right away!
facts.pt: A Lua fica a cerca de 384.400 km, então uma mensagem de rádio leva uns 1,3 segundo para chegar. A Terra pode ajudar quase na hora!
facts.quote: The Moon is an average of 238,855 miles (384,400 kilometers) away.

facts.en: A lander on the Moon measured about 13 microgray of radiation every hour. That is a bit more than inside the space station, and there is no air or magnetic field to stop solar storms.
facts.pt: Uma sonda na Lua mediu cerca de 13 micrograys de radiação por hora. É um pouco mais que dentro da estação espacial, e lá não há ar nem campo magnético para segurar as tempestades solares.
facts.quote: We measured an average total absorbed dose rate in silicon of 13.2 ± 1 μGy/hour
facts.source: Zhang et al. 2020, Science Advances, PMID 32978156 (Chang'e-4 LND; peer-reviewed, not a NASA dataset). Abstract checked via Europe PMC API.

facts.en: Mars can be as warm as 20 °C at noon or as cold as -153 °C. Jezero nights are freezing, so heaters need power.
facts.pt: Marte pode chegar a 20 °C ao meio-dia ou -153 °C. As noites em Jezero são geladas, então os aquecedores gastam energia.
facts.quote: as high as 70 degrees Fahrenheit (20 degrees Celsius) or as low as about -225 degrees Fahrenheit (-153 degrees Celsius)

facts.en: A day on Mars is called a sol. It lasts about 24.6 hours, a bit longer than an Earth day.
facts.pt: Um dia em Marte se chama sol. Ele dura cerca de 24,6 horas, um pouco mais que um dia na Terra.
facts.quote: it completes one rotation every 24.6 hours, which is very similar to one day on Earth (23.9 hours)

facts.en: Mars has a thin atmosphere, mostly carbon dioxide. It blocks a little radiation, but you cannot breathe it, so oxygen must be made in the base.
facts.pt: Marte tem uma atmosfera fina, quase toda de gás carbônico. Ela bloqueia um pouco de radiação, mas não dá para respirar, então o oxigênio é feito na base.
facts.quote: Mars has a thin atmosphere made up mostly of carbon dioxide, nitrogen, and argon gases.

facts.en: Martian winds can make dust storms that cover much of the planet. In 2018 one storm turned day into night for the solar-powered rover Opportunity.
facts.pt: Os ventos de Marte formam tempestades de poeira que cobrem boa parte do planeta. Em 2018 uma delas transformou o dia em noite para o robô solar Opportunity.
facts.quote: Occasionally, winds on Mars are strong enough to create dust storms that cover much of the planet.
facts.source: NASA Science: Mars Facts (Opportunity 2018 storm: NASA/JPL, reported by NPR 13 Jun 2018)

facts.en: Radio messages between Earth and Mars take from about 3 to about 22 minutes one way, depending on where the planets are. Earth cannot answer right away!
facts.pt: Mensagens de rádio entre a Terra e Marte levam de uns 3 a uns 22 minutos para ir, dependendo de onde os planetas estão. A Terra não responde na hora!
facts.quote: about 3 minutes light time … or about 22.4 minutes, depending on the planets’ position in their orbits

facts.en: Jezero Crater is 45 km wide. More than 3.5 billion years ago it held a lake with a river delta. That makes it a great place to look for signs of ancient life.
facts.pt: A cratera Jezero tem 45 km de largura. Há mais de 3,5 bilhões de anos ela tinha um lago com um delta de rio. Por isso é um ótimo lugar para procurar sinais de vida antiga.
facts.quote: Jezero Crater is 28 miles (45 kilometers) wide

facts.en: NASA's Curiosity rover measured about 0.21 milligray of radiation per day on Mars. That is a bit less than on the Moon, because the thin air and the planet itself block some.
facts.pt: O robô Curiosity da NASA mediu cerca de 0,21 miligray de radiação por dia em Marte. É um pouco menos que na Lua, porque o ar fino e o próprio planeta bloqueiam parte.
facts.quote: average absorbed dose rate 0.21 ± 0.04 mGy/day (dose equivalent ≈ 0.64 mSv/day), Curiosity RAD, ~300 sols
facts.source: Hassler et al. 2014, Science, PMID 24324275 (Curiosity RAD). Number is from the paper's results, not its abstract (see data/MISSING.md).
